core_obligations: Control the image boundary despite noncompactness of R by compact truncations and explicit limiting walls.
Use the graph property of critical surfaces to identify the image region.
Identify sigma=a^2bc and the analyticity threshold with the critical boundary to prove D=Pi(R).
proof_roadmap: Compact truncation and noncompact boundary limits
Algebraic sigma coordinate and critical analyticity threshold
difficulty_reason: The proposition establishes a global phase-space parametrization rather than a local coordinate identity. The author handles a noncompact domain with compact truncations, computes two distinct limiting boundary walls, proves the graph structure of critical surfaces and identifies the algebraic root with the analyticity threshold. This geometric/global argument is independent of the RH X-matrix asymptotic lemma and the final free-energy integration.

dedup.scope: Root identified same-source158691 as X-asymptotics only and related later203735 as CD-lemma only. This task counts the global image/boundary theorem for Pi and D=Pi(R), with sigma=a^2bc. It does not count any matrix asymptotic formula, CD identity or the free-energy theorem. Same-source finite-neighbor comparison is restricted to those concrete conclusions.

compared.difference: Prior claim is an asymptotic formula for the X Riemann-Hilbert matrix. New claim is the exact normalized genus-zero log partition-function limit obtained through additional tau differential, coefficient extraction and integration.
Related later critical-paper Christoffel-Darboux identity is not the free-energy limit theorem.

PM015 is the exact limiting free-energy formula using RH/tau asymptotics. PM016 is a global geometric parametrization and critical-boundary identification proved by Jacobian, compact truncation and limiting image analysis; it is not the same conclusion.
